_purpose: M3 schedule-irregularity test, fixed BEFORE the timing features were ever related to recovery. Before this was written, only the timing features' own distributions were inspected (median 7-night onset SD 1.1 h, IQR 0.8-1.6; correlation with WHOOP sleep_consistency_pct -0.19). No regression of recovery on timing was run.
data: all usable cycles in train + frozen test (forward set excluded), complete cases on the variables below, in time order
primary_hypothesis: Higher variability of sleep onset over the previous 7 nights (onset_sd7_hours, circular SD in hours) predicts LOWER recovery, holding sleep amount and quality fixed (TOTAL effect: HRV and RHR are NOT controlled, because they are a likely pathway).

timing_terms.onset_shift_abs_hours: secondary; |tonight's onset - last night's onset|; two-sided
timing_terms.onset_hours: secondary; onset clock time, hours after 18:00 (05:00 = 29); two-sided

excluded_from_controls: sleep_consistency_pct (WHOOP's own timing measure; would partly control away the effect being tested)

inference.method: moving-block bootstrap over time-ordered rows (refit OLS on each resample)
inference.p_value: two-sided bootstrap p = 2 * min(share of resampled coefs <= 0, share >= 0)
inference.multiple_testing: Holm across the 3 timing terms of the TOTAL-effect model

pass_rule_primary.rule: PASS only if the onset_sd7_hours coefficient is <= -2.0 points per +1 h of SD AND its Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 (so its CI excludes 0). Otherwise FAIL, reported as such.

claims: association in observational data from one person; not causation
